newsitem.title: CHINA: Population of Chinese capital races past target.
newsitem.headline: Population of Chinese capital races past target.

text.p: The population of China's capital has swelled above its target to hit more than 12 million people about 15 years ahead of schedule, the China Daily said on Saturday.
The number of people in Beijing exceeded 12.51 million at the end of 1995, up 1.65 million from 1990, the official newspaper said.
"As a result population control has become a difficult task in the capital," it said.
The city's urban population was spreading into the suburbs, which have also become home to a rapidly growing influx of immigrants from poorer rural areas drawn by the prospect of better paying jobs.
Beijing is believed to have a "floating" population of about 3.0 million rural immigrants and it was unclear whether their numbers were included in the latest city population figure.
However, the average Beijing family now numbered 3.15 people, compared with 3.2 people in 1990, the China Daily said.
China enforces a tough one couple, one child family planning policy in its cities.
